summary: Re-verified the fix in 50e04c0 against reviewer-2026-09-20T015000Z.json's critical finding and all 4 warnings from software-engineer-2026-09-20T020500Z.json. All 6 dispatched checks pass. The web tree had NO automated test despite the reviewer's finding explicitly covering both trees — added tests/components/pendingChallengesIdentity.test.tsx (4 cases mirroring the mobile file, real climberHandle output, real mounted PendingChallenges) and proved it red/green the same way. isSearchableQuery(q) === (exactMatchFilter(q) !== null) holds by construction (isSearchableQuery's body literally is that expression) and I locked it in with a 14-fixture equivalence table plus the anti-enumeration property re-derived directly against the new module (never against the route only). Full regression: pnpm lint clean, pnpm typecheck clean, pnpm test 85 files / 799 passed in 8.85s (752 baseline + 47 new: 4 web PendingChallenges + 41 userSearchQuery + 2 failure-branch), node scripts/hygiene.mjs clean. Every temporary break-then-restore left git diff --stat empty on the touched production file before moving to the next check. Working tree now has exactly 3 new untracked test files and no production code changes, per the 'leave uncommitted for review' convention.

learnings.insight: The critical finding's fix commit added a render test for only ONE of the two trees it fixed (mobile), even though the reviewer's original finding, the fix's own exit criteria ('critical_finding_fixed_both_trees': true), and context/conventions.md all say both trees are live and must be exercised. Nothing in CI or the handoff schema forces test-count parity between trees when a fix commit's own description says 'both'. This is the second time in this loop a 'both trees' claim was true for the code change but not for its test coverage (first time: the original implementation before the reviewer caught it).
learnings.action: When a fix handoff claims 'fixed in both trees' but lists a test artifact for only one, treat the untested tree as an open item, not as covered-by-analogy — even a reviewer's own prior finding said as much about 'verified by code reading' claims. Verifier: grep the test artifacts list against both tree paths before accepting a cross-tree fix as fully verified.

learnings.insight: isSearchableQuery(q) === (exactMatchFilter(q) !== null) is true by construction today (one function calls the other), so a fixture-equivalence test on it can look thorough while actually only re-confirming a tautology. The test still has value — it locks the two functions from ever being independently reimplemented without a compensating test failure, and doubles as an isSearchableQuery regression suite — but a reviewer should not read 'the equivalence test passes' as evidence the two code paths were independently implemented and cross-checked. They are the same code path.
learnings.action: When a 'client gate == server gate' claim rests on one function delegating to the other, say so explicitly in the test's own docstring (done here) so a future reader doesn't mistake the equivalence test for an independent-implementation cross-check.
